name: Spice & Witch — Dusk at Glockmund
language_note: Source authored in English; agents render prose in the player's language at runtime.

player.note: The player is Eliane, an ageless being disguised as a spice merchant. See player/eliane.json.

startup.opening_scene:
Dusk runs down between the steep roofs of Glockmund, and the cobblestones shine, washed by the rain.

You hold the violin case tighter and pull the hood of your cloak a little lower. Your wagon waits at the edge of the road outside the walls, carrying everything you own — cinnamon, clove, pepper, and a small pinch of saffron worth more than a peasant's life.

Far off, the church bell falls like a heavy copper coin into the thin mist. The torches at the gate sway in the wind; two guards are stopping everyone who hopes to get in before the locks come down.

From inside the case, a man's languid voice: "And what will you be tonight — a merchant, or … something else?"

You look down at the case. The gate is getting closer. Time to settle on a story.
opening_choices: Walk straight to the gate and claim to be "a spice merchant from the East"
Sort your spices and coins outside the walls first, and plan your line
Murmur to the one in the case — "Tell me, what do I look like tonight?"
Slip into the shadow of the wall and look for a way in that skips the toll

themes: Disguise: each town means inventing an identity; the more lies, the easier to slip
Thirst: at night you can hear blood moving under skin; restraint and indulgence both have a price
Exposure: bells, holy water, daylight, witch-hunters — this age leaves no room for a girl who never ages
The spirit: the violin in your arms is your only companion, and the one thing you can't sell
design_north_star: An ageless being disguised as a merchant, in each town she only stays three days, must turn spice into silver while no one discovers she never grows old and never lingers in the daytime church.
